leading_positions.synthesis: Three members prefer a single-part B014 prize to Guillermo A. Calvo, John B. Taylor and Michael Woodford. Their shared rationale is that Calvo's time-dependent pricing, Taylor's staggered contracts and policy rule, and Woodford's welfare-based synthesis are separable building blocks of the framework behind modern monetary policy analysis. All three treat the work as mature and stress citation wording that does not claim the baseline model forecasts well. Citations differ in emphasis: Krusell includes wage setting, and Andersson centres the policy-analysis framework and avoids any claim about empirical forecasting. They also share the reservation that eight names are credited, so a three-person cut omits Galí, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets. Andersson moved to B014 from B007 after round 1 openings. Others who list B014 only as an alternative (Dreber Almenberg, Friberg, Hassler, Hjalmarsson) are not counted as supporters. Fredriksson (Woodford, Galí, Gertler) and Friberg (originally Galí rather than Calvo) were the explicit divergent B014 trios in opening proposals, and Friberg's round 1 file moves toward Calvo while still ranking B016 first.

Three members prefer a single-part B032 prize to David H. Autor, Gordon H. Hanson and David Dorn. All three moved to this trio in round 1 (Dreber Almenberg from a two-name proposal, Hjalmarsson and Teorell from versions with Katz). They share the view that the China-shock and local-labour-market evidence is transparent, has been re-examined, and has held up qualitatively even though aggregate magnitude and persistence remain debated. They differ in how much of the task-based conceptual framework the citation should claim. Dreber Almenberg frames it around identified evidence. Hjalmarsson frames it around technology and trade shocks with the China-shock evidence as the identified core. Teorell's wording says 'empirical and conceptual analysis'. Katz's exclusion is acknowledged as a real cost by Hjalmarsson and Teorell. Fredriksson lists B032 as an alternative and says he would lean to Autor and Hanson plus either Katz or Dorn, depending on which strand the citation names. Friberg would also keep Dorn over Katz if B032 were chosen.

Three members prefer a single-part B010 prize to Elhanan Helpman and Marc J. Melitz, with Stephen J. Redding left out as a later and separable quantitative and spatial strand. The shared case is a clean two-person attribution, a precisely identifiable core (Melitz 2003 and Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple), and more than twenty years of firm-level testing. All three accept that Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are uncredited on this ballot, and that the size of selection-based welfare gains depends on functional form (Pareto productivity) and sufficient-statistics results. They draw the same practical conclusion: the citation should rest on the selection and reallocation mechanism, not on a welfare magnitude, and Fredriksson adds that it should not claim discovery of the exporter-premia facts. Strömberg moved to B010 from B006. Enflo holds her preference somewhat less firmly than in her opening because of B032's broad support. Andersson and Krusell list B010 only as an alternative.

Two members, Friberg and the chair, prefer a single-part B016 prize to Torsten Persson, Guido Tabellini and Timothy Besley. The chair's opening proposal was Persson and Tabellini only, and he added Besley in round 1 on Friberg's argument that state capacity is a distinct strand. Both treat B016 as field-creating work combining formal theory with empirical evidence, with about three decades of extension. Both name the same reservations: partly observational cross-country identification of constitutional and electoral-rule effects, and partial overlap with the 2024 institutions prize. They describe the breadth of the citation differently. The chair's wording is 'building modern political economics', while Friberg's is narrower and about how constitutions, electoral rules and state capacity shape fiscal policy. Friberg regards a two-person Persson-Tabellini award as defensible and Besley as the most contestable part of his proposal. Fredriksson, Strömberg and Teorell list B016 as an alternative. Dreber Almenberg ranks it third and does not list it as an alternative.

areas_of_agreement: Every member's round 1 file proposes a single-part prize with one ballot ID. Eleven explicit preferences split 3 for B014, 3 for B032, 3 for B010 and 2 for B016. No position approaches the six votes required, and no member prefers a combination of ballots.

Within each leading position, supporters name the same laureate set (B014: Calvo, Taylor, Woodford; B032: Autor, Hanson, Dorn; B010: Helpman, Melitz; B016: Persson, Tabellini, Besley). Remaining disagreement within a position concerns exclusions and citation wording, not the core names.

Most members move toward narrower, more attributable credit lines in round 1 and say they weigh attribution cleanliness and evidential credibility over support counts. Several explicitly decline to treat opening rankings or first-place counts as evidence of merit.

Members across all four positions agree that citations should avoid overclaiming. Examples are no claim of forecasting performance for B014, no specific welfare magnitude for B010, no whole-task-theory claim for B032, and programme-specific rather than whole-field wording for B016.

B042 (John Moore and Nobuhiro Kiyotaki) is listed as an alternative by eight members (Boppart, Dreber Almenberg, Enflo, Hassler, Hjalmarsson, Krusell, Strömberg, Teorell), though no member now prefers it as the single part. Those who discuss it agree its two-person attribution is the cleanest on the list. Their reservations are that the collateral channel is better established as theory than by direct identification, and the possible overlap with the 2022 prize.
No member's preferred ballot is scientifically dismissed by another. Objections are comparative and concern attribution, identification, timing or overlap.
scientific_disputes: B014: Members disagree on how much the post-2008 and 2021-23 inflation episodes bear on the framework. Krusell and Boppart treat them as tests of empirical performance, not of the contribution. Dreber Almenberg and Andersson treat the Phillips-curve slope and parameterisation as an open caveat that should shape citation wording. Fredriksson notes mixed Phillips-curve evidence.

B032: The aggregate magnitude and long-run persistence of China-shock effects, and the inference properties of shift-share exposure designs, are contested. Supporters say the qualitative local-adjustment findings have survived re-examination. Dreber Almenberg and Teorell acknowledge their knowledge of the latest re-examinations is incomplete.

B010: Quantitative work (Pareto assumption, sufficient-statistics results) may imply smaller welfare gains from selection than first claimed. Supporters separate the selection and reallocation mechanism from the gains magnitude. Dreber Almenberg ranks B010 below B032 because quantitative welfare effects depend more on functional form than reduced-form designs do.

B016: Cross-country evidence on constitutional and electoral-rule effects rests partly on observational variation. Dreber Almenberg holds this more strictly than the quasi-experimental local designs in B032, while Friberg rests the case on the formal framework and later sharper designs. Krusell wants the identification issue resolved before ranking B016 above macro candidates.

B042 (alternative only): It is disputed whether the collateral-constraint mechanism has been identified causally or is mostly theory and calibration, with Teorell, Dreber Almenberg and Hassler flagging weaker direct empirical grounding.
attribution_disputes: B014 lists eight names. Any three-person cut leaves out Galí (NK Phillips curve, policy analysis), Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets. Krusell, Boppart and Andersson prefer originators of the building blocks, while Fredriksson's opening favoured Woodford, Galí and Gertler. Whether to honour the theoretical originators or the estimation strand is unresolved.

B014, Calvo versus Galí: Krusell, Andersson and Friberg's round 1 file favour keeping Calvo, with Friberg conceding Calvo is the more identifiable origin. Andersson would give Galí more weight than his own proposal does.

B014, Gertler and the 2022 prize: Andersson and Krusell state that the 2022 prize went to Bernanke, Diamond and Dybvig, not to Gertler, and correct Friberg's opening premise. This is members' stated recollection and is not independently verified here. They would leave Gertler out for strand-separation and cap reasons.

B032, third name: Dorn (co-originator of the local-labour-market design) versus Katz (skill-premium and education-technology strand). Hjalmarsson, Teorell, Dreber Almenberg and Friberg favour Dorn for a trade-shock citation. Fredriksson would lean Autor and Hanson plus either, and Hjalmarsson, Dreber Almenberg and Teorell acknowledge Katz's exclusion as a real cost.

B032, task framework: Credit for the task-based theory also rests on people outside this ballot (Levy, Murnane, Acemoglu, Restrepo). Whether the task framework and the trade-shock evidence are one achievement or two is unresolved, with Acemoglu already recognised in 2024.

B010: Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, whose closely related work is uncredited here, are an acknowledged attribution gap. Enflo, Fredriksson and Strömberg would manage it through citation wording about the theoretical mechanism and by acknowledging that lineage in background documentation. Redding is excluded by all three B010 supporters as a separable later strand.

B016: Whether Besley's state-capacity work is a distinct achievement warranting inclusion (Friberg, chair in round 1) or the weakest link (Friberg's own concession, chair's opening two-name proposal). Acemoglu, Robinson (already recognised) and Alesina sit outside the three-name cut.

B042 (alternative only): Whether Gertler should be added to Kiyotaki and Moore. Teorell and Hjalmarsson now argue for the two-person core because the accelerator lineage is tied to Bernanke, who is not on the ballot.
maturity_disputes: No supporter of B014, B010 or B016 argues that their candidate is immature (about 40 years, 20+ years and about 30 years respectively). Krusell calls B014 arguably overdue, which is a statement about timing, not about credit division, as the chair noted in his reply.

B032 is the most recent leading candidate (core papers about 2003-2016). Supporters hold that 10 to 20 years of replication and re-examination is sufficient, even with magnitude and persistence debated. Others have not argued it is premature.

Overlap with recent prizes is disputed. B016 and the 2024 institutions prize: partial or distinct (Friberg, chair) versus a more material overlap (Dreber Almenberg, Andersson, Fredriksson). B032 and recent labour or technology recognition (Card, Angrist and Imbens, Goldin, Acemoglu 2024): Dreber Almenberg regards the Goldin and Card overlap as not serious, while Hjalmarsson and Teorell flag it. B014 and earlier macro prizes (rational expectations, DSGE, time series): Krusell and Boppart say distinct, Andersson and Fredriksson list it as a concern. B042 and the 2022 prize: complementary or redundant, unresolved.
B010: Krugman's 2008 prize covers earlier new trade theory. Enflo, Fredriksson, Strömberg and Andersson read the heterogeneous-firm strand as distinct and not an increment.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Chair John Hassler prefers B016 and lists B042 and B014 as alternatives. His profile documents no co-authorship or institutional tie to Persson, Tabellini or Besley. His own file notes a possible, unverified IIES connection with Persson that is not in the supplied profile. His dynamic political-economy work is adjacent to the B016 field, and none of those co-authors is credited on a shortlisted ballot. Disclosed, not adjudicated.

Hassler co-authored with Boppart (epi-econ paper), Friberg (menu-costs paper, with Tore Ellingsen) and frequently with Krusell. Boppart and Krusell prefer B014, where Hassler lists B014 only as an alternative, and Friberg prefers B016. None of the three is a credited candidate. Disclosed, not adjudicated.

Boppart and Krusell are frequent co-authors, and both are IIES colleagues of Hassler. Boppart also has a long-running collaboration with Peter Klenow (B030, not in his configuration). Krusell's heterogeneous-agent work is adjacent to non-shortlisted candidates. None of the credited B014 names is a documented co-author of either.

Friberg discloses that his spouse is a political party leader, which he regards as having no apparent bearing, but B016 is a political-economy topic and he prefers it. His field (industrial organisation) is closest to B044, which he ranks lower.

Teorell's research field (comparative democratisation, quality of government) is adjacent to B016, and his 2024 presentation speech concerned institutions and prosperity. He notes the speech may reflect collective drafting and does not establish a personal preference. He lists B016 as an alternative and discloses Stockholm University institutional proximity to Persson.

Strömberg works in corporate finance, close to his opening first choice B006, and treats that as a possible bias on that candidate. He no longer prefers it. Fredriksson discloses an institutional overlap at Stockholm University with the IIES macro group, with no credited B010 name involved. Andersson discloses SSE ties to Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg, with no credited name involved. Enflo's regional-growth research is thematically adjacent to Redding's work and the China-shock literature, and Redding is not in her configuration.

Dreber Almenberg and Hjalmarsson report no apparent conflicts with the candidates in their configurations or alternatives. All flags are disclosed and not adjudicated, and no recusal is proposed or decided here.
questions_for_round2: B014 supporters (Andersson, Boppart, Krusell): If the Committee cannot settle whether it honours the theoretical originators or the estimated medium-scale strand, would you accept a citation confined to nominal-rigidity theory and policy rules? Would you defend Calvo, Taylor and Woodford against a Galí or Gertler substitution on stated criteria, not on opening-support counts?

B032 supporters (Dreber Almenberg, Hjalmarsson, Teorell): Should the citation cover the trade-shock evidence only, with Autor, Dorn and Hanson, or also the task and skill-premium framework, which would strengthen Katz's claim and raise the Levy, Murnane, Acemoglu and Restrepo attribution problem? What specific re-examination evidence on shift-share inference and persistence supports calling it mature?

B010 supporters (Enflo, Fredriksson, Strömberg): How should the Committee weigh the uncredited Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum lineage and the quantitative welfare-gains debate? Would a citation restricted to the selection and reallocation mechanism be accepted by members who prefer other candidates? If the Committee recognises trade at all, is B010 the cleaner strand than the competing candidates (B003, B041, which are outside the shortlist)?

B016 supporters (Friberg, Hassler): Does a Persson-Tabellini two-person award or a three-person award including Besley better match the stated attribution criteria, and how does the state-capacity strand differ from the 2024 institutions prize? Which identification caveats must a citation carry for members who hold observational evidence to a stricter standard?

Cross-candidate: Each member is asked to state, for their own preferred part and for their listed alternatives, what specific evidence or citation change would move them to support another candidate. Given that no position has more than three explicit supporters, which common criteria should separate positions of broadly similar maturity: attribution cleanliness, identification credibility, breadth of consequence, or overlap with recent prizes?

B042 is the most frequent alternative (eight members) but nobody's preferred part. Do supporters of the four leading positions regard it as a better option than the others, and what resolves the 2022-prize overlap and the weaker direct identification of the collateral channel? Should it be elevated or dropped as a fallback?
summary.chair_observation: The round 1 files show four stable positions with no majority and no position near six explicit supporters: B014, B032 and B010 with three each, and B016 with two. Within each position the laureate set is nearly identical, so disagreement is about citation scope, exclusions and cross-field comparison and not about core names. The chair prefers B016, which is among the smaller positions, and this summary counts only explicit round 1 statements. Several moves (Andersson, Teorell and Strömberg changing first choice, plus the Dorn, Katz and Besley revisions) show members responding to attribution and identification arguments, not to support counts. Prior-prize facts, such as the 2022 and 2024 prizes and Gertler's status, are members' stated recollections and have not been independently verified here.
